newsitem.title: POLAND: POLAND CLEARS EIGHT FIRMS FOR DUTY-FREE CAR PARTS.
newsitem.headline: POLAND CLEARS EIGHT FIRMS FOR DUTY-FREE CAR PARTS.

text.p: Poland's foreign trade ministry has granted permits to eight car producers to import duty-free parts, as required by new regulations, and three others should get them soon, a ministry spokesman said on Friday.
Zbigniew Ostrowski said Volvo Poland, Volkswagen Poland, General Motors Poland, Ford Poland and Daewoo-FSO and Daewoo-Lublin, had received permits on Thursday or Friday.
So had Scania Poland and Polish firm Jelcz, he added.
The Polish unit of Fiat Spa got a permit on Wednesday.
Ostrowski told Reuters that three applications for permits had not yet been processed because they were incomplete, but he declined to name the firms involved.
"There are three applications left and we have asked the firms to supplement them. If they do this quickly we can even issue the permits today," Ostrowski said.
Early last week the government adopted a regulation obliging carmakers, as of August 24, to secure permits from the ministry to import duty-free parts for assembly.

The regulation, which was not immediately made available to news media, replaced a previous one which automatically exempted any company from duty on imported parts if it assembled more than 1,000 units annually.
It surprised car makers, threatening those holding low stocks of parts with a temporary halt in production.
